context.ocr_content:
Channel: #desktop-support

09:02 Robin
After yesterday's update the helper launches correctly, but macOS asked for Accessibility permission again. I removed the old entry, added the application from /Applications, and restarted it.

09:05 Ellis
Was the update signed with the same Developer ID identity? Accessibility consent is associated with the application's code-signing requirement, not merely its filename.

09:08 Robin
This was an internal ad-hoc build. The bundle identifier stayed the same, but codesign reports Signature=adhoc. The previous build was also ad-hoc, although it came from a different checkout.

09:11 Ellis
That explains the repeated consent. Ad-hoc signatures do not give us a stable designated requirement across rebuilt artifacts. For public distribution we need Developer ID Application signing, hardened runtime, notarization and stapling. Keep the bundle identifier stable as well.

09:16 Robin
Understood. Separate issue: after granting permission, completions work in TextEdit but the ghost text appears above the baseline in Discord. The AX bounds for the focused element describe the whole editor, while the Chromium text marker bounds describe the caret more accurately.

09:21 Ellis
The overlay should be positioned before inference begins. First use parameterized AX bounds for the insertion range. If Chromium does not expose those, retain the last stable caret rectangle and update it from observed typing advances. Do not move the overlay in response to every noisy measurement.

09:26 Robin
We added a short stabilization window and the bouncing mostly disappeared. There is still a one-pixel shift when accepting a word because the overlay estimates the space width using the system font rather than the editor font.

09:32 Ellis
Use the measured caret position after insertion as the new anchor. The accepted text becomes real editor content, so its resulting AX caret rectangle is a better source of truth than reconstructing glyph advances ourselves.

09:38 Robin
That fixed the acceptance jump. Now we are profiling inference. Decode is fast, but the request is recreated after nearly every character. System instructions, application metadata and most OCR text are unchanged. Only the final input fragment grows.

09:42 Ellis
Measure cold prefill separately from longest-prefix reuse. A server with a block cache should reuse every complete matching block and recompute only the changed tail. Report TTFT rather than generation tok/s because suggestions are fewer than eight words.

09:47 Robin
Current measurements on the M4 Air: first request 640 ms TTFT, identical repeat 188 ms, and appending one character varies between 190 and 510 ms. The variance suggests cache reuse is not consistent near token boundaries.

09:51 Ellis
Run the same request sequence through upstream MLX, oMLX and llama.cpp. Keep the prompt bytes, maximum token count, temperature and stop strings identical. LM Studio can be included as a packaged-runtime control, but it is not something we can embed.

09:55 Robin
Makes sense. I will also capture cache-hit tokens where the API exposes them and record process memory after warmup. For quality, I have regressions covering assistant voice, prompt-label leakage and malformed partial words.

10:01 Ellis
Good. Please post the raw JSON results and a short table. For the first pass, do not add screenshots or clipboard data to the production path; we need explicit privacy controls before enabling those contexts by default.
